summary_hint: Borrower LOE from Dana Lee dated 07/12/2026 — childcare provided by a relative at no cost; no monthly childcare expense; expected to continue.

typed_core.name: borrower_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — flags a bad name split

typed_core.name: letter_date
typed_core.why: processor — recency; ties the explanation to a file state

typed_core.name: current_childcare_expense
typed_core.prompt_hint: Childcare expense is a recurring obligation considered in DTI/residual income for some programs (notably VA residual income); capture the monthly figure, do not decide inclusion. Treat an explicit $0 as a real value, not a null

typed_core.name: expense_frequency
typed_core.why: disambiguator — monthly vs weekly vs annual; the expense is unreadable without it

typed_core.name: payer_name
typed_core.why: processor — who pays (borrower vs third party)

typed_core.name: arrangement_start_date
typed_core.why: processor — how established the arrangement is

typed_core.name: no_expense_reason
typed_core.why: processor — why $0 is claimed (relative care, spouse at home)
typed_core.prompt_hint: A $0 / relative-provided arrangement is a valid outcome — the LOE exists precisely to document the absence of an expense; no_expense_reason carries it

typed_core.name: future_arrangement_or_change_explanation
typed_core.why: processor — narrative of the upcoming change

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: the borrower is the author; no third-party source

rejected.name: borrower_signatures_and_dates
rejected.reason: signature block; attestation carried by borrower_certification; no rule reads individual signatures

rejected.name: dependents_or_children
rejected.reason: sensitive child object[]; replaced by a flat dependent_count to minimize child PII (see Open questions)

rejected.name: supporting_documents
rejected.reason: string[] of exhibits; no consumer; catch-all

encoding_variations: current_childcare_expense / expense_frequency — '$800/mo', '$200/week', '$9,600/yr', or '$0'; always carry the frequency, and treat an explicit $0 as a real value, not a null
no_expense_reason vs expense amount — a letter either states an amount or explains why there is none; capture whichever is present, do not force both
arrangement_type — 'daycare center', 'grandmother watches them', 'nanny', 'after-school program'; drives whether the expense is expected to continue

open_questions.q: dependents_or_children — count vs list vs omit
options: flat dependent_count int (recommended — supports the explanation, no child PII)
nested list with a child-data redactor (heavy plumbing, exposure)
open_questions.recommendation: flat dependent_count int; the number of children covered is the only fact a processor needs GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): dependent_count only — no child names, ages, or DOBs (the prompt hard-blocks child PII).

open_questions.q: $0 expense representation — current_childcare_expense = 0 with no_expense_reason populated, vs a null amount
open_questions.recommendation: store an explicit 0 so the absence is a positive fact, not a missing value

open_questions.q: expected_future_expense — kept because a childcare cost that begins after closing can affect residual income
open_questions.recommendation: confirm this is in-scope for the programs the engine targets, else drop to catch-all

notes: No rules consume this type today, so there is no rule floor. A childcare LOE explains a monthly childcare expense (or its absence) for DTI/residual-income purposes. The load-bearing facts are the expense amount, its frequency, and the arrangement — captured while minimizing sensitive child data.

Repeating lists: none. dependents_or_children is the only repeating candidate, but it is sensitive child data (the catalog's own mortgage_use says 'minimize sensitive child data'). Recommendation: capture a flat dependent_count (int, processor) instead of a list, and never type child names/DOBs. This field is NOT in the typed core table and is carried only in the open question.

PII: no masked identifiers in the catalog for this doc. The real PII risk is child data (names, ages, DOBs of dependents). None is a typed field, and the prompt must hard-block child identifiers from the catch-all. payer_name / childcare_provider_name are standard. Nothing needs _PII_FIELDS registration — but flag child-data handling for the PII reviewer.
Prompt hint (doc-level): Do NOT extract children's names, ages, DOBs, or school names into any field, including the catch-all — record only a count if needed.
Ambiguity: current_childcare_expense is tagged 'headline' (not a defined reason_class); classified as processor (the DTI/expense figure).
